action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 IgG positive (titre 1:80), read with the CSF; moderate hyponatraemia (sodium 129 mEq/L); thyroid, neuronal-surface and onconeural antibodies negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the serum work-up: blood count, chemistry, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV, beta-hCG and a cell-based serum anti-GluN1 IgG assay read together with the CSF result
action_criteria.rationale: Screens metabolic, endocrine, infectious and pregnancy-related contributors and pairs the serum antibody with the decisive CSF assay; here it uncovers moderate hyponatraemia.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Subtle left hippocampal FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion, enhancement or mass effect; no structural lesion
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP; it is normal in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (14 cells/uL) with borderline IgG index; HSV-1/2 PCR negative; CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titre 1:160)
action_criteria.label: Analyse CSF for cells, protein and glucose, oligoclonal bands or IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay
action_criteria.rationale: The CSF anti-GluN1 cell-based assay is the decisive test (Graus 2016 definite criteria), and HSV PCR addresses the infectious mimic that must not be missed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Diffuse slowing with right anterior temporal rhythmic delta; no seizure or extreme delta brush on the routine record
action_criteria.label: Obtain an EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, including extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: An abnormal EEG is one of the Graus 2016 supporting findings, and the staring spells need electrographic characterisation.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left ovarian 3.8 cm complex cystic mass with fat and calcification, consistent with a mature cystic teratoma
action_criteria.label: Screen for an ovarian teratoma with pelvic and abdominal ultrasound
action_criteria.rationale: Women of reproductive age carry the highest teratoma risk; tumour removal is part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG to quantify seizure burden while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist
action_criteria.rationale: Staring spells with right temporal rhythmic delta after a generalised seizure suggest seizures the routine record missed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum osmolality 265 mOsm/kg with urine osmolality 412 mOsm/kg and urine sodium 46 mmol/L
action_criteria.label: Measure serum and urine osmolality (with urine sodium) to characterise the hyponatraemia
action_criteria.rationale: Sodium below 130 mEq/L needs its own work-up; low serum osmolality with inappropriately concentrated urine and urine sodium above 30 mmol/L defines SIADH before fluid restriction or hypertonic saline.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Quetiapine to be stopped (neuroleptic intolerance, seizure threshold); sertraline adds to the low sodium
action_criteria.label: Check the patient's medications against the drugs the acute plan needs (aciclovir, corticosteroids, IVIG, antiseizure medication)
action_criteria.rationale: She started quetiapine 2 days ago and takes sertraline, so the check guides antipsychotic withdrawal and the hyponatraemia review.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1-2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Arrange prompt surgical removal of the left ovarian teratoma (laparoscopic, ovary-sparing where feasible) as part of first-line treatment, with gynaecology.
Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam or lacosamide; avoid valproate in a woman able to become pregnant; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.
Admit to a neurology ward with seizure precautions and continuous cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation, insomnia and catatonia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first; stop quetiapine and monitor CK and temperature.
Treat the moderate hyponatraemia (129 mEq/L) as SIADH after review of sertraline: fluid restriction, correcting by no more than 10 mEq/L in 24 hours.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioural management; gynaecology for the teratoma.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

accepted: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis with left ovarian teratoma

differential.key_features: CSF HSV-1/2 PCR negative three weeks after onset; MRI without haemorrhage or restricted diffusion; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B or AMPA receptor)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA) and onconeural antibodies negative; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Primary psychiatric disorder (acute stress reaction with psychotic features, first-episode psychosis)
differential.key_features: The generalised seizure, staring spells with right temporal seizures on continuous EEG, orofacial dyskinesias, intermittent mutism and CSF pleocytosis are not explained by a primary psychiatric disorder.
Quetiapine only 2 days before the seizure; temperature 37.6 C, CK 148 U/L, normal tone; no clonus to suggest serotonin toxicity; the illness began weeks before quetiapine.

key_clinical_evidence: Three weeks of subacute behavioural change, insomnia, intermittent mutism, a generalised seizure and orofacial dyskinesias: four of the six Graus 2016 groups.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titre 1:160) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive (1:80) is read with the CSF.

MRI shows only subtle left hippocampal FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion or haemorrhage; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds of patients and here excludes HSV encephalitis and structural causes.
Routine EEG shows diffuse slowing with right temporal rhythmic delta, and continuous EEG captures right temporal seizures; extreme delta brush is absent, which excludes nothing.
Pelvic ultrasound shows a 3.8 cm left ovarian mature cystic teratoma: its removal is part of first-line treatment. Moderate hyponatraemia (129 mEq/L, SIADH pattern) needs its own correction.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumour removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis alongside the psychiatric change mandate exclusion of anti-NMDAR encephalitis before a psychiatric diagnosis is accepted.
red_herrings.data_point: Acute psychiatric presentation (insomnia, paranoia, labile mood) in a young postgraduate student with generalised anxiety disorder under academic stress.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatraemia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis. Here sertraline may contribute.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing (SIADH from another cause, dehydration, polydipsia) instead of recognizing SIADH as a known complication of NMDAR-E.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: NMS requires antipsychotic exposure with lead-pipe rigidity, hyperthermia and markedly elevated CK; after 2 days of quetiapine, a CK of 148 U/L with normal tone and temperature 37.6 C reflects the seizure and dyskinesias.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Raises concern for neuroleptic malignant syndrome or rhabdomyolysis when combined with dyskinesias and hyperthermia.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Sertraline does not cause the progressive cognitive decline, seizures, and CSF changes seen here. Anxiety is extremely common and psychiatric history is a known cause of diagnostic delay in anti-NMDAR encephalitis. The 3-week subacute course with seizures and orofacial dyskinesias is beyond an SSRI adverse effect.
red_herrings.data_point: Active SSRI (sertraline) prescription and prior anxiety history
red_herrings.intended_effect: SSRI-related acute psychiatric decompensation or serotonin syndrome

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Antipsychotics may partially suppress psychiatric symptoms of anti-NMDAR encephalitis but do not treat the underlying autoimmune process. New-onset seizures in a first-episode psychosis presentation should always prompt encephalitis workup.
red_herrings.data_point: GP-prescribed quetiapine for a provisional acute stress reaction with psychotic features
red_herrings.intended_effect: First-episode psychosis (schizophrenia spectrum) responding to antipsychotic

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses. Here CSF HSV PCR is negative, the MRI shows no haemorrhage or restricted diffusion, and a CRP of 8 mg/L is non-specific.
red_herrings.data_point: Mild CRP elevation (8 mg/L) and viral prodrome 5 weeks prior

sequence_constraints.reason: Imaging before LP in a patient with seizures or altered consciousness; CT head is an acceptable alternative, so the constraint is soft.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure 18 cmH2O. Mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (WBC 14 cells/uL, 87% lymphocytes) with protein 0.52 g/L and normal glucose (3.6 mmol/L, ratio 0.68). contraindications: Haloperidol and other high-potency D2 antagonists: class warning for severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions in suspected autoimmune encephalitis.
interactions: Quetiapine: dopamine and serotonin antagonist; lowers the seizure threshold, prolongs QTc and carries a risk of neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions; severe neuroleptic intolerance is reported in suspected autoimmune encephalitis. Discontinue and use a benzodiazepine for agitation.
Sertraline: SSRIs are associated with SIADH and hyponatraemia; review the indication when serum sodium is low. Small additive QTc effect with quetiapine.
Methylprednisolone (high dose): hyperglycaemia, hypokalaemia, mood and sleep disturbance; no pharmacokinetic interaction with the current medicines.
Levetiracetam: no clinically relevant interaction with the current medicines; behavioural adverse effects are recognised.
Aciclovir: no interaction with the current medicines; dose by renal function and maintain hydration.
general.proposed: Aciclovir, methylprednisolone, IVIG, levetiracetam; review of current quetiapine and sertraline
warnings: Monitor for neuroleptic malignant syndrome after antipsychotic exposure: hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability, rising CK.
Screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before rituximab.

Occasional bifrontal sharp transients, not clearly epileptiform.
No extreme delta brush pattern. No generalised spike-and-wave. No clear electrographic seizures captured during this recording.

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titres related more closely to outcome than serum titres.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumour, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumour removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Extreme delta brush was found in 7 of 23 adults with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis and was associated with a more prolonged illness.
Severe intolerance to antipsychotics (rigidity, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions) was frequent in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis who received them.
results.source: Lejuste F et al. Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2016;3:e280

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumour removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

patient.history_present_illness: A 27-year-old postgraduate student was brought to the emergency department by her flatmates who had become progressively concerned over the preceding three weeks. She had initially complained of difficulty sleeping, describing lying awake for hours despite exhaustion, and had begun making unusual statements that seemed paranoid in nature, telling her flatmates she believed her supervisor was trying to steal her research data. Her mood had become labile, with episodes of intense agitation alternating with periods of apparent emotional flatness. One flatmate noted that during conversations she would sometimes stop mid-sentence and stare blankly for 10-15 seconds before resuming, which she appeared to have no memory of afterwards. Two days before presentation she was seen by her GP who, noting the insomnia, paranoia, and emotional dysregulation in a young woman under significant academic stress, prescribed low-dose quetiapine 50 mg at night with a provisional diagnosis of acute stress reaction with psychotic features and arranged urgent psychiatry follow-up. However, on the morning of admission her flatmates witnessed a generalised tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately 90 seconds, after which she was post-ictally confused and combative. Apart from generalised anxiety, she had no prior psychiatric illness or psychiatric admission, no prior seizures, and no significant past medical history. She had no family history of psychiatric disease. She had received her HPV and meningococcal vaccines as an adolescent. She takes sertraline 50 mg daily prescribed three months ago by her GP for generalised anxiety related to her PhD. She drinks approximately 10 units of alcohol per week and has no illicit drug use. She is sexually active with a male partner and uses barrier contraception only.

neurological_exam.coordination: Limited assessment. Finger-nose on left side appears intact.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 4mm equal and reactive to light. Extraocular movements full but patient intermittently demonstrates subtle orofacial dyskinesias: lip smacking and tongue protrusion noted on repeated observation. Fundoscopy normal.
neurological_exam.gait: Not assessed: patient in bed, combative when mobilisation attempted.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Agitated and uncooperative. Disoriented to time and place. Intermittent mutism lasting several seconds. Cannot follow complex commands. Mini-mental state examination not formally assessable. Inappropriate affect.
neurological_exam.motor: Power 5/5 in all limbs. Normal tone. No focal weakness.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Symmetrically brisk throughout. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Cannot be formally assessed: patient uncooperative. Withdraws to pain bilaterally.
